requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: A systemd unit file /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled, and started. systemctl status confirms Active: active (running), Loaded/enabled, with the worker process and its child sleep process running under the unit's cgroup.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated 'inventorysvc' account
requirements.summary: inventorysvc was created as a system account (useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin) that did not previously exist (id inventorysvc failed pre-creation). The unit specifies User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps directly shows both the worker process (PID 1950) and its sleep child (PID 1952) running as inventorysvc, not root.

requirements.requirement: Service is managed (enabled to start automatically, not just a one-off process)
requirements.summary: systemctl enable --now was used, and systemctl is-enabled reports 'enabled' both immediately after setup and again after a full reboot, confirming persistence is configured and effective.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes are fully satisfied: os-comparison-worker runs as the systemd-managed 'inventory-worker' service under a newly created, dedicated 'inventorysvc' system account, directly confirmed via ps and systemctl status both before and after a full node reboot. As an independent check (not part of the public contract), the executor also ran the node-restart evidence protocol on node1 with good rigor: a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id aad96cc9…, active/enabled), an explicit reboot acknowledgement, connection timeouts consistent with a genuine disruption, a differing post-restart boot_id (362b323a…), and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service and its correct user context. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, which independently show the boot-identity change and no failed services or package-health issues after executor work.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so restart-evidence coverage across 'every managed node' reduces to a single-node check.
The worker binary is a synthetic sleep-loop script, so there is no persistent data or downstream consumer state to validate beyond process/service status.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a clean, minimal sequence: read-only inspection (cmd-c0bee47cd2564478, cmd-d25cc3cb5b1047b1), user creation (cmd-ac38480d64dc4fc7), unit creation/enable/start (cmd-77a15aef96ca45b5), and verification (cmd-ca376377bdf94468). Every state-changing command maps directly to the task outcome. The reboot-evidence protocol added one minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created because 'nohup systemctl reboot' redirected its output there before backgrounding (cmd-f2c2f7fbb5a144a6); this file remained in the after-executor temp-file snapshot. It is a low-risk, expected byproduct of safely issuing a reboot over a session that would otherwise disconnect, not an abandoned experiment, so it only lightly affects the score. No failed services, no package-health regressions, and no unexplained listening sockets were introduced (only PIDs changed across the reboot, as expected). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found.
